findings.title: TypeScript consumers depend on a hand-written shadow of checked JavaScript policy

evidence.note: One ambient file manually declares five wildcard JavaScript modules, duplicates ConfigSurfaceEntry across two module blocks, and restates max-lines policy and codec shapes.
The checked-JavaScript codec explicitly routes TypeScript consumers through the ambient declaration instead of exposing a declaration derived from its JSDoc contract.

evidence.measurement: 113 lines declare 5 wildcard modules; 10 non-test production TypeScript files directly import one of those modules, measured with rg over the pinned tree excluding test/spec/test-helper and declaration files.
evidence.note: The hand-maintained bridge serves lint coverage, path policy, ratchet, codemod, config-surface, and max-lines tooling.

findings.problem: Runtime policy lives in checked JavaScript while TypeScript consumers compile against an independently authored ambient model. Contributors must synchronize semantic types across runtime validation or JSDoc, a distant wildcard declaration, and bespoke shallow-parity machinery; adopters of the public harness reference inherit the same custom bridge.
findings.proposedDirection: Generate declarations from the checked JavaScript/JSDoc contract or establish one declaration-emitting policy-data boundary consumed by both ESLint config and TypeScript scripts, retaining only a thin binding if module resolution still requires one.

findings.title: Path-policy gives single-segment glob two incompatible private grammars

evidence.note: Changed-file policy exposes a selector explicitly named single-segment-glob.
Its private matcher escapes question marks and brackets and translates only asterisks.
The fixture analyzer calls a pattern a glob when it contains an asterisk, question mark, or opening bracket.
A second single-segment compiler translates asterisks and question marks, passes bracket syntax into RegExp semantics, and refuses globs in directory segments.
Loop-list parsing relies on the fixture compiler and then separately rejects anything still recognized as glob-shaped.

findings.problem: Within one module family, the same vocabulary denotes different languages and failure behavior. Contributors extending changed-file selectors or fixture analysis must discover which punctuation is literal, supported, RegExp-like, or rejected in each implementation.
findings.proposedDirection: Define one documented segment-pattern codec and matcher, or give deliberately narrower dialects distinct types and names; share it with lint-coverage machinery only where the semantics truly match.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The prior fixture-analyzer work documented composition and annotation vocabulary; this identifies conflicting path-pattern languages spanning the changed-file query and fixture analyzer.

findings.title: Bulk codemod modes write one target at a time instead of building one plan

evidence.note: runOne creates its own project, scans all package files, and writes its plan immediately.
The --all mode loops over independently writing runOne operations, repeating package discovery and project construction for each barrel.
Each shared-schema single run creates a fresh project and writes its router and target pair.
Its --all mode preflights only discovery errors before looping over the independently validating and writing single-target operation.

findings.problem: The reusable-looking bulk modes are orchestration loops over single-target commands rather than cohesive bulk operations. They repeatedly construct projects and scan files, expose intermediate repository states, and make contributors reason about recovery target by target instead of reviewing one complete plan.
findings.proposedDirection: Separate analysis from commit: use one project, validate every target, merge plans with collision detection, and invoke the shared writer once after the complete bulk plan succeeds.

findings.title: The debt-log union uses the absence of a discriminator as an entry kind

evidence.note: Accepted-debt entries are the only persisted union variant without a kind field.
Four entry variants require four predicates; accepted debt is recognized indirectly through acceptanceReason.
The parser routes every absent or unrecognized kind through the accepted-debt schema.
Classification and rendering repeat predicate chains instead of using an exhaustive discriminated-union switch.

findings.problem: A persisted four-variant event family lacks a uniform discriminator. Adding an entry kind requires coordinated schema, predicate, parser, classification, and rendering edits, while TypeScript cannot provide straightforward exhaustive dispatch. The historical kind-less shape has become the current authoring contract rather than an isolated compatibility path.
findings.proposedDirection: Write new accepted-debt records with an explicit kind, isolate compatibility parsing for existing kind-less version-1 lines, and dispatch normalized records through exhaustive kind switches.
